study_identification_part.si4_title: Structural brain abnormalities and aggressive behaviour in schizophrenia: Mega-analysis of data from 2095 patients and 2861 healthy controls via the ENIGMA consortium

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To investigate the associations of individual-level deviations from normative values of grey matter volume and white matter microstructural integrity with concurrent aggressive behaviour in schizophrenia, and to examine whether these associations are mediated by positive symptoms, impulse control, and illness insight.

rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.answer: FreeSurfer (structural MRI; Desikan-Killiany atlas for 34 cortical and 7 subcortical regions); Tract-based spatial statistics (TBSS) with John Hopkins University atlas for WM tracts; FMRIB Software Library (FSL); ENIGMA harmonised protocols for image processing and quality control
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.reason: The methods section explicitly describes the preprocessing software and atlases used. The ENIGMA protocols were followed for harmonised processing and QC across sites.
rci7_preprocessing_pipeline.supporting_text: All 20 sites acquired high-resolution (voxel size of ≤ 1 mm³) T1-weighted magnetic resonance imaging scans and processed these using FreeSurfer. Based on the Desikan-Killiany atlas, structural measures were extracted for 34 cortical regions (cortical thickness [CT] and surface area [SA]) and 7 subcortical regions (volume) in each hemisphere. Nine sites also acquired diffusion-weighted images. From these images, values of fractional anisotropy (FA) and mean diffusivity (MD) were extracted for 25 WM tracts in each hemisphere. This was done using tract-based spatial statistics in conjunction with the John Hopkins University atlas, implemented in FMRIB Software Library. Additionally, sites extracted global (whole-brain) measures of CT, SA, FA and MD. The ENIGMA protocols (https://enigma.ini.usc.edu/protocols/), harmonised across sites, were followed for image processing and quality control.

rci9_site_effect_handling.detail: Site included as a predictor variable in warped Bayesian linear regression (wBLR) normative models using PCNtoolkit v0.25. Site was selected as a predictor for statistical reasons to account for site-related variance. Sex and age were also included as predictors for theoretical reasons, and global IDPs were included as predictors for local IDPs. The normative models derived from healthy controls were then applied to patients to calculate individual-level z-score deviations.
rci9_site_effect_handling.supporting_text: For every IDP, we derived a normative model in the healthy controls using warped Bayesian linear regression with site, sex, age and -for local IDPs only -a global IDP as predictors. The predictors were selected for statistical (site) or theoretical (sex, age and global IDPs) reasons. The global IDPs that served as predictors can be found in Table S2. The normative models were then run in the patients to calculate how much they deviated (in z-scores) from healthy controls on an individual level. Normative modelling was performed with the Predictive Clinical Neuroscience toolkit v0.25.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis:
Answer: Ordinal regression models to estimate associations between z-score deviations and aggressive behaviour (ORs with 99% CIs, testwise α=0.01); One-sample t-tests to assess group-level deviations from normative values (z=0); Full mediation analyses using generalised structural equation modeling for delusions, hallucinations, disorganised thinking, poor impulse control, and lack of illness insight (estimating paths X→M, Mx→Y, Xm→Y, X→M→Y); Sensitivity analyses: (1) examining CT, SA, FA, MD components separately; (2) adjusting for current antipsychotic dosage, duration of illness (DOI), and lifetime substance use disorder (SUD) one at a time using OLS regression; (3) restricting outcome to PANSS P7 only

Negative Answer Category: Not Negative
Reason: The statistical analysis section comprehensively describes all association and mediation analyses, including specific methods, covariates, and sensitivity analyses.
Supporting Text: Ordinal regression models were used to estimate the associations between such deviations and aggressive behaviour... To control for multiple testing, we set the testwise level of statistical significance at 1% instead of the more conventional 5%... We performed a full mediation analysis (estimating paths Mx⟹Y, Xm⟹Y and X⟹M⟹Y) for an IDP if it was significantly (at the 1% level) associated with both a potential mediator and aggressive behaviour. For the mediation analyses, we used generalised structural equation modelling... We conducted three sets of sensitivity analyses. First, we examined the components of cortical GM volume (CT and SA) and WM microstructural integrity (FA and MD) individually. Second, we adjusted the analyses -one at a time -for current antipsychotic dosage, DOI and lifetime SUD... Finally, we restricted the outcome to PANSS item P7

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Answer: Greater reductions in total cortical volume and global white matter integrity were significantly associated with increased aggressive behaviour in schizophrenia, with additional regional effects in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, inferior parietal lobule, and internal capsule; most associations were largely mediated by increased positive symptoms and reduced impulse control, suggesting a neurobiological basis for the co-occurrence of these clinical features.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Answer: Aggressive behaviour was significantly associated with reductions in total cortical volume (OR [99% CI] = 0.88 [0.78, 0.98], p = .003) and global white matter microstructural integrity (OR [99% CI] = 0.72 [0.59, 0.88], p = 3.50 × 10⁻⁵), and additional region-specific reductions in dorsolateral prefrontal cortex volume (OR [99% CI] = 0.85 [0.74, 0.97], p = .002), inferior parietal lobule volume (OR [99% CI] = 0.76 [0.66, 0.87], p = 2.20 × 10⁻⁷), and internal capsule integrity (OR [99% CI] = 0.76 [0.63, 0.92], p = 2.90 × 10⁻⁴). All these IDPs except internal capsule integrity showed significant group-level reductions in patients versus controls. Mediation analyses revealed that except for inferior parietal lobule volume, these associations were largely mediated by increased severity of positive symptoms (delusions, hallucinations, disorganised thinking) and reduced impulse control. Specifically: delusions mediated TCV (OR=0.94, p=3.00×10⁻⁴), global WM integrity (OR=0.83, p=1.10×10⁻⁴), and DLPFC volume (OR=0.93, p=3.20×10⁻⁴); hallucinations mediated TCV (OR=0.96, p=3.60×10⁻⁴) and global WM integrity (OR=0.91, p=.003); disorganised thinking mediated TCV (OR=0.94, p=3.70×10⁻⁴), global WM integrity (OR=0.77, p=5.50×10⁻⁶), DLPFC volume (OR=0.92, p=1.40×10⁻⁵), and IC integrity (OR=0.81, p=1.80×10⁻⁴); poor impulse control mediated TCV (OR=0.86, p=.006), global WM integrity (OR=0.70, p=6.10×10⁻⁵), DLPFC volume (OR=0.84, p=.006), and IC integrity (OR=0.72, p=1.60×10⁻⁴). Results were robust in sensitivity analyses examining CT/SA and FA/MD components separately, adjusting for antipsychotic dosage, duration of illness, and substance use disorder (except IC integrity for SUD), and restricting to PANSS P7 only.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Answer: This is the largest study to date (N=2095 patients) investigating structural brain abnormalities and aggression in schizophrenia, and the first to use individual-level normative modeling rather than group-level case-control comparisons. The multi-site ENIGMA consortium design enhances representativeness. Approximately one in seven patients (15%) displayed mild or more severe aggression. Findings suggest potential clinical applications: (1) candidate neuroimaging markers for predicting treatment response; (2) potential targets for neuromodulation therapies (deep brain stimulation, transcranial magnetic stimulation); (3) support for nonpharmacological interventions with neuroprotective/neurogenic effects (cognitive behavioural therapy, cognitive remediation therapy, physical exercise); (4) rationale for investigating whether structural neuroimaging adds to limited predictive performance of current violence risk assessment instruments. However, authors note modest effect sizes largely mediated by more easily measurable risk factors, emphasizing need to consider benefit-harm balance and cost-effectiveness. Future research should use longitudinal designs to clarify causal mechanisms, test specific cognitive functions as mediators, employ network analyses to understand structural brain networks underlying aggression, and consider theory of mind impairments as potential mediators for inferior parietal lobule findings.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Answer: Cross-sectional design precludes causal inference despite temporal proximity of scanning and aggression measurement; aggressive behaviour measured at single timepoint may attenuate effects as brain abnormalities likely more pronounced in recurrent versus incidental aggression; aggression measured with single items from symptom scales (PANSS, SAPS, BPRS) rather than multi-item purpose-designed aggression instruments; aggressive behaviour and potential mediators measured with same instruments creating risk of inter-item correlation contributing to mediation effects; no information about comorbid antisocial personality disorder or psychopathy which may moderate structural brain correlates of aggression; pairwise region-based analyses may miss network-level effects on aggression; acutely agitated patients difficult to recruit and scan successfully potentially limiting generalisability.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This mega-analysis pooled data from 20 ENIGMA Schizophrenia Working Group sites across 13 countries (COBRE, ESO, FIDMAG, FOR2107, GAP, IGP, IMH, JBNU, MCIC, Montreal, MPRC, NU, Olin, RomeSL, RSCZ, SNUH, UCISZ, UMCU, UNINA, Zürich). The study employed individual-level normative modeling using warped Bayesian linear regression (wBLR) implemented in PCNtoolkit v0.25, with site, sex, age, and global IDPs as predictors. Site effects were handled through model-based inclusion of site as a predictor variable. ENIGMA harmonised protocols were followed for image processing and quality control across sites, though specific QC metrics and exclusion numbers are not detailed in the provided text. The study references published ENIGMA protocols (https://enigma.ini.usc.edu/protocols/) and prior publications for scanner/acquisition details. No explicit validation of the normative models (within-sample CV, independent validation, or external validation) is reported. The study measured aggressive behaviour using standardised psychiatric rating scales (PANSS item P7 [n=16 sites], SAPS item B3 [n=3 sites], or BPRS item 10 [n=1 site]), harmonised to a 6-point scale. Antipsychotic medication use was high (91% of patients), with median chlorpromazine equivalent dosage of 300 mg (IQR=406). Median duration of illness was 7 years (IQR=16). Among patients with available data (37%), 42% had lifetime substance use disorder. This is a medRxiv preprint (posted February 5, 2024) not yet peer-reviewed. The authors declare no financial conflicts of interest. Funding sources for each participating site are detailed in the supplement.
